summary: Application already has a last_decision accessor computing the latest Farmer-subject decision; the new relation carries the same name with different semantics, so was keeping both names the intent?
evidence: app/Models/Application.php:265 already defines getLastDecisionAttribute(), which filters decisionsWithTrashed to subject Farmer and returns the last one; it is read widely as $application->last_decision (for example app/Http/Controllers/Admin/ApplicationActionController.php:163, app/Machines/International/Romania/Application/Actions/SendRejectionNotificationToFarmerAction.php:29). The question is the shared name plus the differing result set. The accessor reads decisionsWithTrashed and so includes soft-deleted decisions, while the relation excludes them, so the two can return different rows for the same application. On top of that, in Laravel 11 (composer.json:30 pins ^11.39.0) Model::getAttribute() tests hasGetMutator($key) before falling through to relations, and Str::studly('lastDecision') is 'LastDecision', so getLastDecisionAttribute() appears to match a property read of $application->lastDecision as well. summary: The subject = Farmer filter is applied to the outer relation query while latestOfMany() picks MAX(id) over all of the application's decisions, so lastDecision may resolve to null for an application that does have farmer decisions.
evidence: latestOfMany() turns this into a one-of-many relation: it builds a fresh subquery on the related model that groups application_decisions by application_id and selects MAX(id), then joins the relation query to it. The ->where('subject', Farmer) added on line 1088 lives on the outer query, not inside that subquery. If the highest-id decision row of an application is a guarantor decision, the join selects that row and the outer subject filter then discards it, so the relation is empty even though farmer decisions exist. Guarantor rows do land in the same table after farmer rows: decisionsForGuarantor() (app/Models/Application.php:1214) reads them, and GuarantorScoreTransition writes subject = Guarantor at app/Services/ApplicationStrategy/ForwardSale/StateMachine/Transitions/GuarantorScoreTransition.php:92, which runs after the farmer decision in the guarantor flow. The repo's other constrained one-of-many relation, Farmer::latestOfficialIdentityDocument() (app/Models/Farmer.php:799), puts its filter inside the ofMany aggregate closure instead. The two new tests do not distinguish the two readings: tests/Unit/Model/ApplicationTest.php:281 creates the farmer decision last, so it already holds MAX(id), and the guarantor-last ordering is never exercised. The visible consequence would be at app/Http/Controllers/Retailer/ApplicationActionController.php:146, where withWhereHas('lastDecision', ...) would silently drop guarantor-bearing applications from the rejected-with-other-reason list. I could not run the query here, so this is asked rather than asserted: is the subject filter meant to be inside the subquery? Adding a fifth decision with subject Guarantor and created_at now() after the farmer decision in it_returns_the_latest_decision() would settle it.

summary: The model already defines getLastDecisionAttribute(), whose mutator name collides with the new lastDecision relation, so property access on $application->lastDecision appears to reach the accessor rather than the eager-loaded relation.
evidence: app/Models/Application.php:265 defines getLastDecisionAttribute(). Eloquent's getAttribute() checks hasGetMutator($key) before falling through to getRelationValue($key), and Str::studly('lastDecision') is 'LastDecision', so the key 'lastDecision' matches that existing mutator. On that reading, $application->lastDecision returns the accessor's value -- the last farmer decision taken from decisionsWithTrashed, which includes soft-deleted rows -- and never the relation loaded from the database. Two consumers read it exactly that way: app/Http/Resources/Retailer/BaseApplicationResource.php:57-63 reads $application->lastDecision->id and siblings as a property, and app/Http/Controllers/Retailer/ApplicationActionController.php:208 eager-loads 'lastDecision:id,application_decisions.application_id,farmer_id,decision,data,subject,type' to feed it. If the accessor wins, that column-limited eager load is never read, decisionsWithTrashed is lazily loaded once per application instead, and a soft-deleted farmer decision can be serialised where the relation would have returned the newest live one. Note also that BaseApplicationResource builds the whenLoaded() array eagerly, so $application->lastDecision->id is evaluated even when the relation is absent. I cannot execute the resolution here to confirm which of the accessor and the relation wins; naming the relation something that does not collide (or removing the accessor) would remove the ambiguity either way.
suggestion: Either drop getLastDecisionAttribute() in favour of the relation, or give the relation a name that does not collide with an existing get*Attribute mutator, so property access resolves to the loaded relation.

summary: No test creates a Guarantor decision as the application's newest decision, so the interaction between the subject filter and the latestOfMany subquery is never exercised.

It creates four decisions in sequence (Farmer at -4d, Guarantor at -3d, Farmer at -2d, Guarantor at now) and then a fifth Farmer decision at -1d, so the row with the highest primary key is always a Farmer decision and the Guarantor rows never hold the maximum. latestOfMany() builds its MAX subquery from a fresh query on the related model, so the ->where('subject', Farmer) placed before it constrains only the outer query, not the aggregate subquery; the relation would then pick the application's newest decision irrespective of subject and drop it when that newest row is a Guarantor decision, yielding null rather than the newest Farmer decision. summary: No test pins which column makes a decision the 'latest', because every arrangement inserts decisions in ascending created_at order so key order and chronological order coincide.

In tests/Unit/Model/ApplicationTest.php:265 the Farmer decisions are inserted at -4d, -2d and -1d, i.e. in ascending created_at order, so the row with the highest key is also the chronologically newest one and the test cannot distinguish the two orderings. A Farmer decision inserted later but backdated — a higher key with an older created_at — would be returned as the 'latest', and no existing test would notice. summary: The filtered collection is handed to ApplicationResource::collection() without re-indexing, so as soon as one application is dropped the response's `data` serializes as a JSON object keyed by the original offsets instead of a JSON array.
evidence:
Path: the query at line 142 runs ->get(), which yields an Eloquent collection keyed 0..n-1 in result order; ->filter() at line 152 preserves those keys; the result goes straight into ApplicationResource::collection() at line 157. AnonymousResourceCollection keeps the keys it is given (mapInto preserves them) and its toArray() returns that keyed array, so json_encode emits an object whenever the keys are not 0..n-1.

Input that reaches it: a retailer with two applications rejected under OtherReasonsRejectionSpecification inside the window, for farmers F1 and F2. F1 has since started another application at the same retailer, F2 has not. The SQL returns [0 => appF1, 1 => appF2]; the filter drops key 0; the body is {"data":{"1":{...}}} rather than {"data":[{...}]}. Any consumer doing data.length / data.map / Array.isArray on the list sees a different shape than on the all-pass case.

Why the new tests do not catch it: in a_retailer_can_view_rejected_applications_with_other_reason nothing is filtered out (keys stay sequential); the other three new tests assert an empty list, and json_encode of an empty array is still []. The gap only opens when at least one row is dropped and a later row survives.

Other occurrence of the same rule in head, checked: waitingApplications() in the same file (lines 113-131) filters the same way before WaitingApplicationResource::collection() and also omits the re-index, so it has the same shape hazard today - that is another copy of the pattern, not evidence, and it may mean the frontend already tolerates object-shaped `data`. I could not run a probe to settle how the consumer reacts, so the defect I am asserting is the response shape itself, not downstream breakage.

Deliberate-choice check: nothing in the diff suggests the object shape is wanted, and the codebase re-indexes in the equivalent places (see citations).
suggestion: Append ->values() after the ->filter(...) closure so the collection handed to ApplicationResource::collection() is re-indexed from zero.

summary: The new lastDecision test arranges a Guarantor decision as the newest row for the application and then expects the older Farmer decision back, but lastDecision() chains ->where('subject', Farmer) before ->latestOfMany(), and a chained where is not carried into the one-of-many aggregate subquery, so the relation may resolve to null here and the test may not pass.
evidence:
The fixture gives the application five decisions: Farmer -4d, Guarantor -3d, Farmer -2d, Guarantor now(), and then a Farmer at now()->subDays() (-1d). The globally newest row by created_at is the Guarantor at now(); the test asserts assertNotNull and assertEquals($decision->id, ...) for the Farmer row at -1d, so it only holds if the aggregate that picks the 'latest' row is itself restricted to subject = Farmer.

app/Models/Application.php:1087-1089 builds the relation as hasOne(Decision::class)->where('subject', ApplicationDecisionSubject::Farmer->value)->latestOfMany(). In Eloquent (laravel/framework ^11.39, composer.json:30) HasOneOrMany::ofMany builds each aggregate subquery from a fresh builder on the related model rather than from the relation's own query, so a where() chained onto the relation before latestOfMany() constrains only the outer joined query, not the MAX(created_at) subquery. That is why the framework exposes the aggregate-closure form, and it is the form this repo already uses for exactly this shape of filter at app/Models/Farmer.php:796-806 (latestOfficialIdentityDocument puts the category filter inside the aggregate closure instead of chaining it).

If that reading is right, the generated query joins application_decisions to a subquery of MAX(created_at) per application_id computed over all subjects, matches the Guarantor row at now(), and the outer subject = 'farmer' predicate then removes it, so $application->lastDecision()->first() returns null and this test fails on assertNotNull. The same semantics would also affect the consumers of the relation: app/Http/Controllers/Retailer/ApplicationActionController.php:146 (withWhereHas('lastDecision', ...) for the rejected-with-other-reason list) would silently skip any application whose newest decision overall is a Guarantor decision, and app/Http/Resources/Retailer/BaseApplicationResource.php:56 would then emit no last_decision block for it.

I cannot run the suite in this measurement, so I cannot settle whether the test passes; the experiment that would settle it is running these two test methods, or dumping Application::first()->lastDecision()->toSql() and checking whether the aggregate subquery carries a subject predicate. Other one-of-many relations in the head, all checked: app/Models/Product.php:350 (tarfinProPrice) and app/Models/Order.php:492 (latestFinancingCost) chain no filter and are unaffected; app/Models/Farmer.php:799 already uses the closure form. lastDecision is the only one that chains a where before the aggregate.

The author may have arranged the Guarantor-at-now() row deliberately to prove that guarantor decisions are excluded, which is the right thing to test; the question is only whether the relation as written actually produces that result.
suggestion: If the test does fail, move the subject filter into the aggregate so it constrains the MAX as well, mirroring Farmer::latestOfficialIdentityDocument: hasOne(Decision::class)->ofMany(['created_at' => 'MAX', 'id' => 'MAX'], fn (Builder $query) => $query->where('subject', ApplicationDecisionSubject::Farmer->value)); the test as arranged then passes unchanged.

summary: The fixture of it_returns_the_latest_decision makes the expected row the last one inserted, so the test may not distinguish lastDecision() from a plain latest decision of any subject.

Discriminating it needs a Guarantor-subject row inserted after the expected Farmer row (higher id), so that dropping the filter selects the Guarantor row and the assertion on $decision->id fails.
suggestion: Create the expected Farmer decision first and a Guarantor decision last (higher id, later created_at), then assert lastDecision()->first()->id equals the Farmer row's id; that arrangement fails if the subject filter is removed.

In the resource, last_decision is emitted through whenLoaded('lastDecision', ...) (app/Http/Resources/Retailer/BaseApplicationResource.php:56), so the expected key list built from the unloaded model omits last_decision. Expected and actual therefore move together: with line 208 removed the relation is unloaded, the key disappears from the response, the expected list still omits it, and the assertion still holds. Two consequences follow. First, nothing checks that the column list on line 208 is the right one - if a column the resource reads (id, application_id, farmer_id, decision, data, subject, type) were dropped or misspelled in this select, no assertion would notice. Second, the boundary case this change exists for is never reached: Application::factory()->withRetailer()->withOrder()->create() adds no ApplicationDecision (database/factories/ApplicationFactory.php - decisions only arrive via states such as rejectedWithReason() at :351 or withRejectionDecision() at :372), so in both tests the eager-loaded relation resolves to null and the populated branch is never exercised. evidence: PHP evaluates the second argument of whenLoaded before whenLoaded runs, so the seven $application->lastDecision->... reads happen regardless of what whenLoaded later returns. lastDecision (app/Models/Application.php:1085) is a hasOne(Decision::class)->where('subject', Farmer)->latestOfMany(), so it can be loaded and still null for an application that carries no farmer-subject decision, and ApplicationActionController::baseApplication loads 'lastDecision:...' unconditionally for every application it serves (ApplicationActionController.php:208) rather than through the withWhereHas guard used by rejectedApplicationsWithOtherReason (ApplicationActionController.php:146). Whether an application reaching the view-base endpoint can actually have an empty lastDecision is not something I can establish by reading alone, which is why this is asked rather than asserted: if it can, the array literal raises on null before whenLoaded ever returns MissingValue. Wrap the array in the closure form already used by ApplicationResource, so the relation is only read once whenLoaded has decided it is present:

            'last_decision' => $this->whenLoaded('lastDecision', fn (): array => [

                'farmer_id'      => $application->lastDecision->farmer_id,

summary: The `last_decision` array is passed to `whenLoaded` as a literal, so `$application->lastDecision->id` is dereferenced before `whenLoaded` can guard it, and every application with no farmer-subject decision makes GET base-application fail with "Attempt to read property on null".
evidence: PHP evaluates the second argument of `whenLoaded` at the call site: the array at lines 57-63 is fully built, including `$application->lastDecision->id`, before `whenLoaded` is entered, so neither of the guards inside `whenLoaded` (relation-not-loaded, relation-is-null) can protect these seven property reads. `lastDecision()` is a `hasOne(Decision::class)->where('subject', Farmer)->latestOfMany()` (app/Models/Application.php:1085), and the repository's own unit test `it_returns_null_if_no_decision_exists` (tests/Unit/Model/ApplicationTest.php:299) records that it is null for an application with no decision. `ApplicationActionController::baseApplication()` loads the relation unconditionally (app/Http/Controllers/Retailer/ApplicationActionController.php:208), and `ApplicationPolicy::viewBase()` (app/Policies/Retailer/ApplicationPolicy.php:33) gates only on retailer and sales channel, not on status, so any of the retailer's own applications reaches this code -- including a freshly created one in PROTOCOL_WAITING/AD_WAITING, which has no `application_decisions` row at all. After the eager `load()`, `relationLoaded('lastDecision')` is true and the value is null, so execution reaches `null->id` and the endpoint returns a 500 instead of the resource. The path is also exercised by the PR's own feature tests: `a_retailer_can_view_a_base_application` (tests/Feature/Retailer/ApplicationActionControllerTest.php:1906) and `a_retailer_can_view_a_base_application_with_sales_channel_id_query_param` (line 1929) build the application with `Application::factory()->withRetailer(...)->withOrder()->create()`, and neither the factory `definition()`/`configure()` nor `withOrder()` creates a decision (database/factories/ApplicationFactory.php:59, :156, :252) -- only the explicit states `rejectedWithReason()`, `withRejectionDecision()` and `withRetailerAnomaly()` do. I could not run those tests here, so I did not confirm the failure by execution. Other occurrences of the same predicate in the file: the `farmer` branch (line 22) dereferences `$farmer->...` the same way, but `farmer` is a required belongs-to that line 18 already reads unconditionally; the `company` branch (line 51) is safe because it uses `$application->company?->tin` -- the new branch is the only one that dereferences a nullable relation without a guard. I also checked every other `whenLoaded` call under app/ : all the ones with a computed value use a closure (e.g. app/Http/Resources/Admin/ApplicationResource.php:19, app/Services/DualGuard/Resources/DualGuardedActionResource.php:25, app/Services/PreApprovedLimit/Resources/Admin/PreApprovedLimitApplicationDecisionResource.php:21), which is exactly the form that defers the dereference; this unit is the only array-literal case that touches a relation property.
suggestion: Wrap the value in a closure so it is evaluated only when the relation is loaded and non-null: `'last_decision' => $this->whenLoaded('lastDecision', fn (): array => ['id' => $application->lastDecision->id, ...])`, matching the closure form already used elsewhere in the codebase.

evidence: Application::lastDecision() (app/Models/Application.php:1085) is a HasOne scoped to subject=Farmer with latestOfMany(), so it is null for an application with no decisions and also for one whose decisions are all Guarantor-subject - the second case is constructed in tests/Unit/Model/ApplicationTest.php:265 for the model, never for this resource. summary: The new guard reads the last decision through the `last_decision` accessor, while every other machine action that inspects the last decision uses `decisions()->forFarmer($application->farmer)->latest()->first()`; was the different reader chosen deliberately?
evidence: The comparison itself follows the codebase idiom: `->type === class_basename(SomeSpecification::class)` appears in roughly forty places, so the diff is not reinventing that. What differs is how the decision is fetched. `SendMissingInfoNotificationToSMAction`, which runs in the same `REJECTED_TRANSITION` action list of `App\Machines\International\Romania\Application\ApplicationMachine` (`RejectAction`, `CreatePreApprovedLimitAction`, `SendMissingInfoNotificationToSMAction`, then this action), reads `$application->decisions()->forFarmer($application->farmer)->latest()->first()`; so do `App\Machines\Application\Actions\SendMissingInfoNotificationToSMAction` and `SendRejectedNotificationByReasonAction`. This unit instead reads the `last_decision` appended accessor, which is `Application::getLastDecisionAttribute()`: it resolves through the `decisionsWithTrashed()` relation (`hasMany(Decision::class)->withTrashed()`), filters on subject Farmer, and returns `$decisions->last()` — that is, the last element in relation load order, not an ordered `latest()`. Two semantic differences follow from that: soft-deleted decisions participate (the admin flow does soft-delete decisions, see `Http/Controllers/Admin/ApplicationActionController.php` checking `$application->last_decision->deleted_at`), and the winner is decided by relation ordering rather than by `latest()`. A third reader also exists, the `lastDecision()` HasOne relation (`latestOfMany()` with subject Farmer, no trashed rows), which is what `Http/Controllers/Retailer/ApplicationActionController.php` uses for the same OtherReasons check. The staleness hazard I first suspected does not apply: `GettableContextProperty::__call()` calls `refresh()` by default, which reloads loaded relations, so the decision `RejectAction` just created is visible. I could not run anything here, so whether the trashed-inclusive, unordered reader was a deliberate choice is a question for the author, not a defect I can assert. The identical line in `SendRejectionNotificationToRetailerAction.php:29` carries whatever answer applies here.
suggestion: If the intent is "the decision this rejection just wrote", the sibling idiom `$application->decisions()->forFarmer($application->farmer)->latest()->first()` (or the `lastDecision` relation the retailer controller uses for the same OtherReasons check) states it without pulling soft-deleted rows in, and keeps the two actions of this transition reading the decision the same way.

summary: The new "do not notify the farmer when the rejection reason is OtherReasons" rule is applied only on the v4 (EventMachine) Romania rejection path; the legacy Romania strategy rejection path still notifies the farmer unconditionally, so it is unclear whether that path is still reachable for a Romania application rejected for other reasons.
evidence:
The rule the claim describes is "a rejection whose last farmer decision is OtherReasonsRejectionSpecification must not produce an ApplicationRejectedNotification to the farmer". Romania has two live rejection routes, and the change covers one of them.

Route A (changed): an AD rejection on a v4 application goes through Admin\ApplicationActionController::transition, which at line 378 takes the isV4() branch and sends the status event into application_mre. In the Romania machine that lands on REJECTED_TRANSITION (app/Machines/International/Romania/Application/ApplicationMachine.php:99-108), where RejectAction persists the decision with type = the payload's reason type and subject Farmer before SendRejectionNotificationToFarmerAction runs, so the new guard sees the fresh decision (getApplication() refreshes the model by default, GettableContextProperty.php:29-30) and correctly suppresses the notification.

Route B (not changed): the same controller's else branch (lines 386-391) drives a non-v4 application through $application->state()->transitionTo(...). For the Romania sales channels, Navigator still maps that to the legacy strategies (Navigator.php:32-34), whose rejected transitions list SendRejectionNotificationToFarmer as a completion action (PrivateIndividual RejectedTransition.php:46 and ForwardSale RejectedTransition.php:38), and that completion action calls $application->farmer->notify(new ApplicationRejectedNotification($application->id)) with no reason check at all (SendRejectionNotificationToFarmer.php:19). An AD rejecting a non-v4 Romania application with reason type OtherReasonsRejectionSpecification would therefore still send the farmer the rejection notification the claim says should be suppressed.

What I could not settle from the tree: whether any Romania application without an application_mre can still reach a rejection. Romania applications created through Retailer\RomaniaApplicationMachineController::start get an application_mre, but Retailer\SalesChannelApplicationController::create still reaches Navigator::fire for any sales channel id, and older Romania applications sitting in AD-waiting would take Route B. That is a data/rollout fact, not something the diff shows, which is why this is a question rather than a finding.

Other occurrences of the predicate I searched and checked: SendRejectionNotificationToRetailerAction.php:29 carries the identical guard and is changed in the same way, so the retailer side of Route A is consistent. The Turkey v4 path (Machines/Application/Actions/SendRejectedNotificationToFarmerAction.php, reached from RejectedEntryAction.php:20) is unguarded, but OtherReasonsRejectionSpecification is listed only under allowed_ro in config/application-decisions.php:20-26, which Admin\ApplicationActionController::reasons resolves per current country at line 205, so that reason cannot be chosen for a Turkey application and no gap exists there. The InterState and MobileForwardSale SendRejectedNotificationToFarmer actions belong to the Turkey sales channels for the same reason.

If the legacy Romania strategy is already dead for new rejections, this needs no change; if it is not, the same guard belongs in SendRejectionNotificationToFarmer (and in its retailer counterpart in the same directory).
